For canonical positive integers simultaneously palindromic in bases b and b^k, b,k>=2, the proof separates L=kq (q>=1) into palindromic k-blocks in palindromic block order, giving (b-1)b^{ceil(k/2)ceil(q/2)-1}, from L=kq+r (q>=0,1<=r<k), where base-b^k and base-b palindromicity force a width-r palindromic payload A_0, repeated zero prefixes of length k-r before further width-r palindrome payloads A_i, and palindromic payload list. The recursive stripping argument is valid for internal padded blocks without imposing canonical leading-digit restrictions after the first. Count is (b-1)b^{ceil(r/2)ceil((q+1)/2)-1}; independent geometric-pair summation gives the stated rational generating function. The largest free dimension ceil(k/2) per two full blocks yields Theta(X^{ceil(k/2)/(2k)}); picking a full-block length multiple of 2k below log_b(X) supplies the lower bound, and uniform geometric bounds across residues the upper. Independent arithmetic direct base conversion and count checked 92 bounded base/k/length profiles; inspected symbolic dimension checker. Infinite validity rests on block reasoning.

Beyond the elementary fact that infinitely many exist, this result characterizes *all* simultaneous palindromes for every integer power pair, gives exact counts by digit length and a complete rational generating function, plus the growth exponent. These are natural counting invariants of a fundamental numeral condition, not isolated trivially tiny values, even if the counting techniques are elementary.
